title: Rebekah
summary: Rebekah is an ancestral figure in Genesis whose life advances promise, family, and covenant formation.
historical_context: Rebekah belongs to the ancestral world of Genesis, where clans, migration, inheritance, and land promise shape the story.
ancient_near_east_context: Kinship loyalty, household religion, and inheritance customs form the background of the patriarchal narratives.
literary_context: Genesis uses Rebekah to connect promise to Israel's earliest family story.
covenantal_significance: Rebekah participates in the promise line that later culminates in Israel, David, and Christ.
interpretive_notes: Read the figure as part of a family and promise line, not as an isolated biography.
The family narratives frequently combine faith, failure, and divine promise in the same story.
common_questions: Why does this figure matter in Genesis?
